stops.note: literally 'vine of the dead/spirit' (aya spirit + waska vine), naming the psychoactive vine brew
Quechua 'vine of the soul', from 'aya', spirit, plus 'waska', rope
stops.meaning: a psychoactive brew made from the vine and other plants

stops.note: entered English through anthropological and later popular accounts of Amazonian ceremonies
stops.meaning: a psychoactive brew used in traditional Amazonian spiritual ceremonies

current_meaning: a psychoactive plant brew used in traditional and modern Amazonian spiritual ceremonies
